sectors.trend: Gold names outperform on multiple WA discoveries and Auric's $28M profit; copper (True North) and lithium (ZhongNuo/Chariot) exploration active; oil spike from Persian Gulf tanker fires supports energy miners
sectors.implications: Gold and energy miners (GOLD.AX, WES.AX, BHP.AX) benefit from safe-haven flows and oil volatility; base-metals names face mixed signals from Chinese solar overtaking coal

sectors.trend: CBA faces reputational damage from 13-year inactive-card fee saga; rate-hike expectations support NIM but mortgage stress at 18-year highs threatens credit quality; Bathla collapse signals property-sector stress
sectors.implications: Big Four (CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX) face margin pressure from credit losses vs. NIM gains; REITs and property developers under pressure

sectors.trend: Persian Gulf tanker fires spike crude; domestic energy transition costs 'running off the rails'; One Nation pushes to keep coal plant open; gas cartel scrutiny (Beetaloo)
sectors.implications: Woodside (WDS.AX) and Santos (STO.AX) benefit from oil spike; coal names face political headwinds; renewable transition cost overruns weigh on utilities

sectors.trend: Qantas strike vote threatens QAN.AX; Costco service disruption; dining chain Chapter 11; small-business uncertainty post-Covid; period poverty and grocery theft signal consumer stress
sectors.implications: QAN.AX faces industrial-action risk; consumer discretionary names under pressure from mortgage stress and cost-of-living squeeze

sectors.trend: Nvidia signals AI boom continues; Marvell/Google deal uncertainty; Citi recommends buying tumbling tech; Canva privacy legal fight; HCA Healthcare and Elevance Health show US healthcare resilience
sectors.implications: ASX tech (CNA.AX, W1.AX) benefits from global AI momentum; CSL.AX and SGH.AX track US healthcare peers positively

sectors.trend: House prices face potential 10% fall; mortgage stress at 18-year highs; Bathla near collapse; Melbourne councils admit inability to cope with population growth; YIMBY policy debate
sectors.implications: Property REITs (GPW.AX, DGL.AX, ICPS.AX) face valuation pressure; construction and infrastructure names may benefit from housing supply push

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce REIT and property exposure; increase allocation to rate-sensitive growth equities; hedge with long-duration bonds

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Qantas industrial action and property developer defaults
risk_assessment.mitigation: Avoid QAN.AX near-term; monitor Bathla and broader property credit; favour cash-rich industrials

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Productivity deterioration and 'toxic cocktail' market blow-up
risk_assessment.mitigation: Maintain cash buffers; diversify into gold and defensive healthcare; avoid over-leveraged positions

risk_assessment.risk_factor: CBA fee controversy and banking sector reputational risk
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor CBA.AX for regulatory action; diversify across Big Four; watch for consumer sentiment shift

opportunities.recommendation: Add energy exposure on Persian Gulf oil spike
opportunities.rationale: Tanker fires in Gulf create supply shock; WDS and STO benefit from elevated crude; gas cartel scrutiny supports pricing power

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce property and REIT exposure ahead of potential 10% house-price correction
defensive_moves.rationale: Mortgage stress at 18-year highs, Bathla near collapse, fourth rate hike loom; housing supply constraints in Melbourne add structural risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid Qantas and consumer discretionary near-term
defensive_moves.rationale: Strike vote creates binary risk; consumer stress from cost-of-living and mortgage pressure weighs on discretionary spend

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain 10-15% cash allocation as hedge against 'toxic cocktail' scenario
defensive_moves.rationale: Productivity 'bad to worse', debt war raging, and geopolitical oil risk create tail-risk; cash provides optionality

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain volatile and range-bound. Oil-driven inflation and rate-hike fears cap upside, while Wall Street strength and gold discoveries provide floor. Expect 2-3% two-way volatility over next 4-6 weeks. CBA fee saga and Qantas strike vote add idiosyncratic risk.
market_outlook.long_term: Structural headwinds from productivity decline, housing correction risk, and energy transition costs cap ASX 200 upside. Gold, energy, and healthcare offer relative outperformance. A 10% house-price correction could trigger broader financial-sector stress. AI/tech remains a global tailwind for ASX-listed tech names.
